NULLNULLNULLNULLNULLNULLNULLExcavatedThese samples were recovered from the Natael Na site in southcentral Alaska. This is in the northern Copper River basin, within the northern unit of Wrangell-Saint Elias National Park and Preserve. The site is located on a low but well-drained loess ridge, believed to have formed over a durable bedrock outcrop. It is adjacent to an interpreted paleo-delta where Tanada Creek entered Glacial Lake Ahtna, which is believed to have persisted until roughly 10,000 cal BP. The top of the landform, including the area the samples were recovered from is at an elevation of roughly 780 meters above sea level. The area is currently a cool, wet boreal forest dominated by white spruce, though birch and aspen are also present at the site. Dwarf birch is common in the surrounding understory and willow is present, though primarily in the low areas surrounding the ridge. The ridgetop where the site is located is covered primarily with Labrador Tea, though some low-bush cranberry is present on the south-facing slope. Other vegetation present in the site area includes bog blueberry, crowberry, kinnikinic, bear berry, artic lupin, and timberberry."""
